Package com.nexuslink.protocol.mqtt

Class MqttTopicFilter

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.mqtt.MqttTopicFilter
public final class MqttTopicFilter extends Object
A pure, dependency-free implementation of MQTT topic matching and topic/filter validation as specified by MQTT 3.1.1 and MQTT 5.0, section 4.7 ("Topic Names and Topic Filters").

A topic name is the concrete label a message is published to (no wildcards). A topic filter is what a subscription registers and may contain the wildcards defined in §4.7.1:

  • + — the single-level wildcard; it must occupy an entire level and matches exactly one level (including an empty level). E.g. sport/+/player1 matches sport/tennis/player1.
  • # — the multi-level wildcard; it must be the last character of the filter and occupy its own level. It matches the parent level and any number of child levels, so sport/# matches sport, sport/tennis and sport/tennis/x, and # on its own matches every topic.

Per §4.7.2 the server MUST NOT match a Topic Filter that starts with a wildcard (# or +) against a Topic Name beginning with $ (e.g. $SYS/...); such topics are only reachable by a filter that names the $-prefixed level explicitly.

Instances are immutable: a filter is compiled once via compile(String) (which validates it) and its pre-split levels are reused for many matches(String) calls. Each match walks the topic string by index without splitting it, so no per-match allocation occurs.
